quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' (pee-lon-go), which sounds like the fluttering motion of wings! Hungary is home to over 160 species of butterflies, and some traditional Hungarian folk costumes feature intricate butterfly embroidery as symbols of transformation and joy.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals in the Salish Sea
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals, like those you can spot from Port Angeles shores, have special whiskers that help them track fish in murky water. Learn about these charming marine neighbors and their surprising abilities.

medium_read.title: The Joy of Cutting Gardens: Growing Flowers for Your Home
medium_read.teaser: Discover how to create a beautiful cutting garden that provides fresh bouquets all summer long. This guide covers easy-to-grow flowers perfect for the Pacific Northwest climate.

long_read.title: The Ancient Art of Hungarian Porcelain: Herend's Story
long_read.teaser: For nearly 200 years, the Herend porcelain factory has created exquisite hand-painted masterpieces that have graced royal tables across Europe. Journey through the history of Hungary's most treasured craft and the artisans who keep these traditions alive.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: This is peak season for spotting Olympic black-tailed deer at Hurricane Ridge, where they graze in the alpine meadows. These gentle creatures are smaller than their mainland cousins and are found only in the Pacific Northwest. Early morning and late afternoon are the best times to see them against the wildflower-filled meadows.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute when active.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! That tiny heart is working incredibly hard — imagine 20 beats every single second!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute when they're flying around.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts beat an amazing 1,200 times per minute — that's 20 beats every second! No wonder they need so much nectar for energy.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any animal on Earth. At night, they enter a state called torpor, slowing their heart rate to just 50 beats per minute to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's perfect — you know your Hungarian greetings!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word for 'thank you' is 'köszönöm' (kuh-suh-nuhm). It's one of the most important words to know in any language!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language that's not related to the surrounding European languages — it's part of the Finno-Ugric family, making it a linguistic cousin to Finnish and Estonian. The formal version of thank you is 'köszönöm szépen' (thank you very much).

puzzle_3.question: What remarkable ability do salmon have that helps them return to their birthplace?
options: They remember the scent of their home stream
puzzle_3.correct_response: That's right! Salmon have an incredible sense of smell that allows them to remember and recognize the unique chemical signature of the stream where they were born, even after years in the ocean.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Salmon actually remember the unique scent of their home stream! They can detect the chemical signature of their birthplace even after spending years in the ocean, guiding them home to spawn.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Salmon in the Strait of Juan de Fuca use this amazing olfactory memory to navigate from the Pacific Ocean back to the exact streams in Olympic Peninsula rivers where they were born. Some travel over 900 miles to return home.
